items.definition: A machine that lifts and lowers a load and moves it horizontally, with the hoisting mechanism built in as part of the machine. Cranes, whether fixed or mobile, are driven manually or by power.
items.quote: A crane is a machine for lifting and lowering a load and moving it horizontally, with the hoisting mechanism an integral part of the machine. Cranes whether fixed or mobile are driven manually or by power.

items.definition: A crane that, when activated, operates through a preset cycle or cycles.
items.quote: An automatic crane is a crane which when activated operates through a preset cycle or cycles.

items.definition: A crane controlled by an operator in a cab located on the bridge or trolley.
items.quote: A cab-operated crane is a crane controlled by an operator in a cab located on the bridge or trolley.

items.definition: A gantry or semigantry crane whose bridge girders or trusses extend crosswise beyond the crane runway on one or both sides.
items.quote: Cantilever gantry crane means a gantry or semigantry crane in which the bridge girders or trusses extend transversely beyond the crane runway on one or both sides.

items.definition: A crane controlled by pendant or nonconductive rope by an operator on the floor or on an independent platform.
items.quote: Floor-operated crane means a crane which is pendant or nonconductive rope controlled by an operator on the floor or an independent platform.

items.definition: A crane similar to an overhead crane, except that the bridge carrying the trolley or trolleys is rigidly supported on two or more legs running on fixed rails or another runway.
items.quote: Gantry crane means a crane similar to an overhead crane except that the bridge for carrying the trolley or trolleys is rigidly supported on two or more legs running on fixed rails or other runway.

items.definition: An overhead crane used to transport or pour molten material.
items.quote: Hot metal handling crane means an overhead crane used for transporting or pouring molten material.

items.definition: A crane with a movable bridge that carries a movable or fixed hoisting mechanism and travels on a fixed overhead runway structure.
items.quote: Overhead crane means a crane with a movable bridge carrying a movable or fixed hoisting mechanism and traveling on an overhead fixed runway structure.

items.definition: A crane whose mechanism is driven by electric, air, hydraulic, or internal combustion means.
items.quote: Power-operated crane means a crane whose mechanism is driven by electric, air, hydraulic, or internal combustion means.

items.definition: A crane operated from a fixed operator station that is not attached to the crane.
items.quote: A pulpit-operated crane is a crane operated from a fixed operator station not attached to the crane.

items.definition: A crane controlled, by any method other than pendant or rope control, by an operator who is not in a pulpit or in the cab attached to the crane.
items.quote: A remote-operated crane is a crane controlled by an operator not in a pulpit or in the cab attached to the crane, by any method other than pendant or rope control.

items.definition: A gantry crane with one end of the bridge rigidly supported on one or more legs that run on a fixed rail or runway, and the other end supported by a truck running on an elevated rail or runway.
items.quote: A semigantry crane is a gantry crane with one end of the bridge rigidly supported on one or more legs that run on a fixed rail or runway, the other end of the bridge being supported by a truck running on an elevated rail or runway.

items.definition: A long-span, gantry-type crane usually used for bulk storage of material, with bridge girders or trusses rigidly or nonrigidly supported on one or more legs. It may have one or more fixed or hinged cantilever ends.
items.quote: Storage bridge crane means a gantry type crane of long span usually used for bulk storage of material; the bridge girders or trusses are rigidly or nonrigidly supported on one or more legs. It may have one or more fixed or hinged cantilever ends.

items.definition: A crane with a jib, with or without a trolley, supported from a building's side wall or line of columns. It is a traveling type that operates on a runway attached to the side wall or columns.
items.quote: Wall crane means a crane having a jib with or without trolley and supported from a side wall or line of columns of a building. It is a traveling type and operates on a runway attached to the side wall or columns.

items.definition: Assigned specific responsibilities by the employer or the employer's representative.
items.quote: Appointed means assigned specific responsibilities by the employer or the employer's representative.

items.definition: The American National Standards Institute.
items.quote: ANSI means the American National Standards Institute.

items.definition: A supplemental hoisting unit with a lighter capacity, and usually a higher speed, than that provided for the main hoist.
items.quote: An auxiliary hoist is a supplemental hoisting unit of lighter capacity and usually higher speed than provided for the main hoist.

items.definition: A device that slows or stops motion by friction or power means.
items.quote: A brake is a device used for retarding or stopping motion by friction or power means.

items.definition: A brake that provides retarding force without external control.
items.quote: A drag brake is a brake which provides retarding force without external control.

items.definition: A brake that automatically prevents motion when power is off.
items.quote: A holding brake is a brake that automatically prevents motion when power is off.

items.definition: The part of a crane, consisting of girders, trucks, end ties, footwalks, and drive mechanism, that carries the trolley or trolleys.
items.quote: Bridge means that part of a crane consisting of girders, trucks, end ties, footwalks, and drive mechanism which carries the trolley or trolleys.

items.definition: Crane movement in a direction parallel to the crane runway.
items.quote: Bridge travel means the crane movement in a direction parallel to the crane runway.

items.definition: An energy-absorbing device that reduces impact when a moving crane or trolley reaches the end of its permitted travel, or when two moving cranes or trolleys come into contact.
items.quote: A bumper (buffer) is an energy absorbing device for reducing impact when a moving crane or trolley reaches the end of its permitted travel; or when two moving cranes or trolleys come in contact.

items.definition: The operator's compartment on a crane.
items.quote: The cab is the operator's compartment on a crane.

items.definition: The distance from any part of the crane to a point of the nearest obstruction.
items.quote: Clearance means the distance from any part of the crane to a point of the nearest obstruction.

items.definition: Contacting devices that collect current from runway or bridge conductors.
items.quote: Collectors current are contacting devices for collecting current from runway or bridge conductors.

items.definition: The electrical conductors located along a crane's bridge structure to provide power to the trolley.
items.quote: Conductors, bridge are the electrical conductors located along the bridge structure of a crane to provide power to the trolley.

items.definition: The electrical conductors located along a crane runway to provide power to the crane.
items.quote: Conductors, runway (main) are the electrical conductors located along a crane runway to provide power to the crane.

items.definition: A method of controlling crane motor speed when the motor is in an overhauling condition.
items.quote: The control braking means is a method of controlling crane motor speed when in an overhauling condition.

items.definition: A control method in which power to the motor is reversed to develop torque in the opposite direction.
items.quote: Countertorque means a method of control by which the power to the motor is reversed to develop torque in the opposite direction.

items.definition: A method of controlling crane motor speeds in the overhauling condition to provide a retarding force.
items.quote: Dynamic means a method of controlling crane motor speeds when in the overhauling condition to provide a retarding force.

items.definition: A form of dynamic braking in which the electrical energy generated is fed back into the power system.
items.quote: Regenerative means a form of dynamic braking in which the electrical energy generated is fed back into the power system.

items.definition: A method of control by friction.
items.quote: Mechanical means a method of control by friction.

items.definition: A controller that returns automatically to a neutral position when released.
items.quote: Controller, spring return means a controller which when released will return automatically to a neutral position.

items.definition: Selected or assigned by the employer or the employer's representative as being qualified to perform specific duties.
items.quote: Designated means selected or assigned by the employer or the employer's representative as being qualified to perform specific duties.

items.definition: A point on a travel motion controller that releases the brake while the motor is not energized, which allows coasting before the brake is set.
items.quote: A drift point means a point on a travel motion controller which releases the brake while the motor is not energized. This allows for coasting before the brake is set.

items.definition: The cylindrical part around which ropes are wound to raise or lower the load.
items.quote: The drum is the cylindrical member around which the ropes are wound for raising or lowering the load.

items.definition: A device that compensates for unequal length or stretch of a rope.
items.quote: An equalizer is a device which compensates for unequal length or stretch of a rope.

items.definition: Capable of being contacted inadvertently. It is applied to hazardous objects that are not adequately guarded or isolated.
items.quote: Exposed means capable of being contacted inadvertently. Applied to hazardous objects not adequately guarded or isolated.

items.definition: A provision designed to automatically stop or safely control any motion in which a malfunction occurs.
items.quote: Fail-safe means a provision designed to automatically stop or safely control any motion in which a malfunction occurs.

items.definition: The walkway with a handrail, attached to the bridge or trolley for access.
items.quote: Footwalk means the walkway with handrail, attached to the bridge or trolley for access purposes.

items.definition: An apparatus, which may be part of a crane, that exerts a force for lifting or lowering.
items.quote: A hoist is an apparatus which may be a part of a crane, exerting a force for lifting or lowering.

items.definition: The load-bearing chain in a hoist.
items.quote: Hoist chain means the load bearing chain in a hoist.

items.definition: The motion of a crane that raises and lowers a load.
items.quote: Hoist motion means that motion of a crane which raises and lowers a load.

items.definition: The total superimposed weight on the load block or hook.
items.quote: Load means the total superimposed weight on the load block or hook.

items.definition: The assembly of hook or shackle, swivel, bearing, sheaves, pins, and frame suspended by the hoisting rope.
items.quote: The load block is the assembly of hook or shackle, swivel, bearing, sheaves, pins, and frame suspended by the hoisting rope.

items.definition: An electromagnetic device carried on a crane hook to pick up loads magnetically.
items.quote: Magnet means an electromagnetic device carried on a crane hook to pick up loads magnetically.

items.definition: The hoist mechanism provided for lifting the maximum rated load.
items.quote: Main hoist means the hoist mechanism provided for lifting the maximum rated load.

items.definition: A trolley with an operator's cab attached to it.
items.quote: A man trolley is a trolley having an operator's cab attached thereto.

items.definition: The maximum load for which the manufacturer designed and built a crane or individual hoist, as shown on the equipment nameplate(s).
items.quote: Rated load means the maximum load for which a crane or individual hoist is designed and built by the manufacturer and shown on the equipment nameplate(s).

items.definition: Wire rope, unless otherwise specified.
items.quote: Rope refers to wire rope, unless otherwise specified.

items.definition: A sheave that rotates as the load block is raised or lowered.
items.quote: Running sheave means a sheave which rotates as the load block is raised or lowered.

items.definition: An assembly of rails, beams, girders, brackets, and framework on which the crane or trolley travels.
items.quote: Runway means an assembly of rails, beams, girders, brackets, and framework on which the crane or trolley travels.

items.definition: The portion of the hoist pull acting horizontally when the hoist lines are not operated vertically.
items.quote: Side pull means that portion of the hoist pull acting horizontally when the hoist lines are not operated vertically.

items.definition: The horizontal distance, center to center, between runway rails.
items.quote: Span means the horizontal distance center to center of runway rails.

items.definition: A crane that is not in regular service but is used occasionally or intermittently as required.
items.quote: Standby crane means a crane which is not in regular service but which is used occasionally or intermittently as required.

items.definition: A device that limits travel of a trolley or crane bridge. It is normally attached to a fixed structure and normally cannot absorb energy.
items.quote: A stop is a device to limit travel of a trolley or crane bridge. This device normally is attached to a fixed structure and normally does not have energy absorbing ability.

items.definition: A device for making, breaking, or changing the connections in an electric circuit.
items.quote: A switch is a device for making, breaking, or for changing the connections in an electric circuit.

items.definition: A manually or automatically operated electric switch that cuts off electric power independently of the regular operating controls.
items.quote: An emergency stop switch is a manually or automatically operated electric switch to cut off electric power independently of the regular operating controls.

items.definition: A switch operated by some part or motion of a power-driven machine or equipment to alter the electric circuit associated with it.
items.quote: A limit switch is a switch which is operated by some part or motion of a power-driven machine or equipment to alter the electric circuit associated with the machine or equipment.

items.definition: A switch that controls the entire power supply to the crane.
items.quote: A main switch is a switch controlling the entire power supply to the crane.

items.definition: A switch that dominates the operation of contactors, relays, or other remotely operated devices.
items.quote: A master switch is a switch which dominates the operation of contactors, relays, or other remotely operated devices.

items.definition: The unit that travels on the bridge rails and carries the hoisting mechanism.
items.quote: The trolley is the unit which travels on the bridge rails and carries the hoisting mechanism.

items.definition: Trolley movement at right angles to the crane runway.
items.quote: Trolley travel means the trolley movement at right angles to the crane runway.

items.definition: The unit consisting of a frame, wheels, bearings, and axles that supports the bridge girders or trolleys.
items.quote: Truck means the unit consisting of a frame, wheels, bearings, and axles which supports the bridge girders or trolleys.

items.definition: The name the text gives to the self-setting brake, at least one of which each independent hoisting unit of a crane must have, applied directly to the motor shaft or some part of the gear train.
items.quote: (i) Each independent hoisting unit of a crane shall be equipped with at least one self-setting brake, hereafter referred to as a holding brake, applied directly to the motor shaft or some part of the gear train.

items.definition: One of the two general classifications of inspection procedure for cranes in regular service, with daily to monthly intervals between inspections. The classifications are based on the intervals at which inspection should be performed, which depend on the nature of the crane's critical components and their exposure to wear, deterioration, or malfunction.
items.quote:
(ii) Inspection procedure for cranes in regular service is divided into two general classifications based upon the intervals at which inspection should be performed. The intervals in turn are dependent upon the nature of the critical components of the crane and the degree of their exposure to wear, deterioration, or malfunction. The two general classifications are herein designated as “frequent” and “periodic” with respective intervals between inspections as defined below:
(a) Frequent inspection—Daily to monthly intervals.

items.definition: One of the two general classifications of inspection procedure for cranes in regular service, with 1 to 12-month intervals between inspections. The classifications are based on the intervals at which inspection should be performed, which depend on the nature of the crane's critical components and their exposure to wear, deterioration, or malfunction.
items.quote:
(ii) Inspection procedure for cranes in regular service is divided into two general classifications based upon the intervals at which inspection should be performed. The intervals in turn are dependent upon the nature of the critical components of the crane and the degree of their exposure to wear, deterioration, or malfunction. The two general classifications are herein designated as “frequent” and “periodic” with respective intervals between inspections as defined below:
(a) Frequent inspection—Daily to monthly intervals.
[29cfr1910.179(j)(1)(ii)(b)] (b) Periodic inspection—1 to 12-month intervals.

items.definition: A rotating superstructure with power plant, operating machinery, and boom, mounted on a base with crawler treads for travel. Its function is to hoist and swing loads at various radii.
items.quote: A crawler crane consists of a rotating superstructure with power plant, operating machinery, and boom, mounted on a base, equipped with crawler treads for travel. Its function is to hoist and swing loads at various radii.

items.definition: A rotating superstructure with power plant, operating machinery and boom, mounted on a base or car equipped for travel on railroad track. It may be self-propelled or propelled by an outside source, and its function is to hoist and swing loads at various radii.
items.quote: A locomotive crane consists of a rotating superstructure with power-plant, operating machinery and boom, mounted on a base or car equipped for travel on railroad track. It may be self-propelled or propelled by an outside source. Its function is to hoist and swing loads at various radii.

items.definition: A rotating superstructure with powerplant, operating machinery and boom, mounted on an automotive truck that has a powerplant for travel. Its function is to hoist and swing loads at various radii.
items.quote: A truck crane consists of a rotating superstructure with powerplant, operating machinery and boom, mounted on an automotive truck equipped with a powerplant for travel. Its function is to hoist and swing loads at various radii.

items.definition: A rotating superstructure with powerplant, operating machinery and boom, mounted on a base or platform with axles and rubber-tired wheels for travel. The base is usually propelled by the engine in the superstructure but may have a separate engine controlled from the superstructure; the crane's function is to hoist and swing loads at various radii.
items.quote: A wheel mounted crane (wagon crane) consists of a rotating superstructure with powerplant, operating machinery and boom, mounted on a base or platform equipped with axles and rubber-tired wheels for travel. The base is usually propelled by the engine in the superstructure, but it may be equipped with a separate engine controlled from the superstructure. Its function is to hoist and swing loads at various radii.

items.definition: A secondary part or assembly of parts that contributes to the overall function and usefulness of a machine.
items.quote: An accessory is a secondary part or assembly of parts which contributes to the overall function and usefulness of a machine.

items.definition: Assigned specific responsibilities by the employer or the employer's representative.
items.quote: Appointed means assigned specific responsibilities by the employer or the employer's representative.

items.definition: The American National Standards Institute.
items.quote: ANSI means the American National Standards Institute.

items.definition: An accessory that measures the angle of the boom to the horizontal.
items.quote: An angle indicator (boom) is an accessory which measures the angle of the boom to the horizontal.

items.definition: The vertical axis around which the crane superstructure rotates.
items.quote: The axis of rotation is the vertical axis around which the crane superstructure rotates.

items.definition: The shaft or spindle with which or about which a wheel rotates. On truck- and wheel-mounted cranes, it refers to an automotive type of axle assembly including housings, gearing, differential, bearings, and mounting appurtenances.
items.quote: Axle means the shaft or spindle with which or about which a wheel rotates. On truck- and wheel-mounted cranes it refers to an automotive type of axle assembly including housings, gearing, differential, bearings, and mounting appurtenances.

items.definition: Two or more automotive-type axles mounted in tandem in a frame so as to divide the load between the axles and permit vertical oscillation of the wheels.
items.quote: Axle (bogie) means two or more automotive-type axles mounted in tandem in a frame so as to divide the load between the axles and permit vertical oscillation of the wheels.

items.definition: The traveling base or carrier on which the rotating superstructure is mounted, such as a car, truck, crawlers, or wheel platform.
items.quote: The base (mounting) is the traveling base or carrier on which the rotating superstructure is mounted such as a car, truck, crawlers, or wheel platform.

items.definition: A member hinged to the front of the rotating superstructure, with its outer end supported by ropes leading to a gantry or A-frame, and used to support the hoisting tackle.
items.quote: The boom (crane) is a member hinged to the front of the rotating superstructure with the outer end supported by ropes leading to a gantry or A-frame and used for supporting the hoisting tackle.

items.definition: The angle between the longitudinal centerline of the boom and the horizontal. That centerline is a straight line between the boom foot pin (heel pin) centerline and the boom point sheave pin centerline.
items.quote: The boom angle is the angle between the longitudinal centerline of the boom and the horizontal. The boom longitudinal centerline is a straight line between the boom foot pin (heel pin) centerline and boom point sheave pin centerline.

items.definition: A straight line between the boom foot pin (heel pin) centerline and the boom point sheave pin centerline.
items.quote: The boom longitudinal centerline is a straight line between the boom foot pin (heel pin) centerline and boom point sheave pin centerline.

items.definition: A hoist drum and rope reeving system used to raise and lower the boom. The rope system may be all live reeving or a combination of live reeving and pendants.
items.quote: The boom hoist is a hoist drum and rope reeving system used to raise and lower the boom. The rope system may be all live reeving or a combination of live reeving and pendants.

items.definition: A device used to limit the angle of the boom at the highest position.
items.quote: The boom stop is a device used to limit the angle of the boom at the highest position.

items.definition: A device used to slow or stop motion by friction or power means.
items.quote: A brake is a device used for retarding or stopping motion by friction or power means.

items.definition: A housing that covers the rotating superstructure machinery and/or the operator's station. On truck-crane trucks, a separate cab covers the driver's station.
items.quote: A cab is a housing which covers the rotating superstructure machinery and/or operator's station. On truck-crane trucks a separate cab covers the driver's station.

items.definition: A friction, electromagnetic, hydraulic, pneumatic, or positive mechanical device for engaging or disengaging power.
items.quote: The clutch is a friction, electromagnetic, hydraulic, pneumatic, or positive mechanical device for engagement or disengagement of power.

items.definition: A weight used to supplement the machine's weight in providing stability for lifting working loads.
items.quote: The counterweight is a weight used to supplement the weight of the machine in providing stability for lifting working loads.

items.definition: Selected or assigned by the employer or the employer's representative as being qualified to perform specific duties.
items.quote: Designated means selected or assigned by the employer or the employer's representative as being qualified to perform specific duties.

items.definition: The cylindrical members around which ropes are wound to raise and lower the load or boom.
items.quote: The drum is the cylindrical members around which ropes are wound for raising and lowering the load or boom.

items.definition: Loads introduced into the machine or its components by forces in motion.
items.quote: Dynamic (loading) means loads introduced into the machine or its components by forces in motion.

items.definition: A structural frame extending above the superstructure, to which the boom support ropes are reeved.
items.quote: The gantry (A-frame) is a structural frame, extending above the superstructure, to which the boom support ropes are reeved.

items.definition: An extension attached to the boom point to provide added boom length for lifting specified loads. It may be in line with the boom or offset to various angles.
items.quote: A jib is an extension attached to the boom point to provide added boom length for lifting specified loads. The jib may be in line with the boom or offset to various angles.

items.definition: The external load, in pounds, applied to the crane, including the weight of load-attaching equipment such as load blocks, shackles, and slings.
items.quote: Load (working) means the external load, in pounds, applied to the crane, including the weight of load-attaching equipment such as load blocks, shackles, and slings.

items.definition: The assembly of hook or shackle, swivel, sheaves, pins, and frame suspended from the boom point.
items.quote: Load block (upper) means the assembly of hook or shackle, swivel, sheaves, pins, and frame suspended from the boom point.

items.definition: The assembly of hook or shackle, swivel, sheaves, pins, and frame suspended by the hoisting ropes.
items.quote: Load block (lower) means the assembly of hook or shackle, swivel, sheaves, pins, and frame suspended by the hoisting ropes.

items.definition: A hoist drum and rope reeving system used to hoist and lower loads.
items.quote: A load hoist is a hoist drum and rope reeving system used for hoisting and lowering loads.

items.definition: Crane ratings in pounds established by the manufacturer in accordance with this section's load rating provisions.
items.quote: Load ratings are crane ratings in pounds established by the manufacturer in accordance with paragraph (c) of this section.

items.definition: Extendable or fixed metal arms attached to the mounting base, which rest on supports at the outer ends.
items.quote: Outriggers are extendable or fixed metal arms, attached to the mounting base, which rest on supports at the outer ends.

items.definition: A tong-like metal device, mounted on a locomotive crane car, which can be connected to the track.
items.quote: Rail clamp means a tong-like metal device, mounted on a locomotive crane car, which can be connected to the track.

items.definition: A rope system in which the rope travels around drums and sheaves.
items.quote: Reeving means a rope system in which the rope travels around drums and sheaves.

items.definition: A wire rope, unless otherwise specified.
items.quote: Rope refers to a wire rope unless otherwise specified.

items.definition: A load applied at an angle to the vertical plane of the boom.
items.quote: Side loading means a load applied at an angle to the vertical plane of the boom.

items.definition: A crane that is not in regular service but is used occasionally or intermittently as required.
items.quote: A standby crane is a crane which is not in regular service but which is used occasionally or intermittently as required.

items.definition: A supporting rope that maintains a constant distance between the points of attachment to the two components it connects.
items.quote: A standing (guy) rope is a supporting rope which maintains a constant distance between the points of attachment to the two components connected by the rope.

items.definition: The ability of the machine and its components to withstand the stresses imposed by applied loads.
items.quote: Structural competence means the ability of the machine and its components to withstand the stresses imposed by applied loads.

items.definition: The rotating upper frame structure of the machine and the operating machinery mounted on it.
items.quote: Superstructure means the rotating upper frame structure of the machine and the operating machinery mounted thereon.

items.definition: Rotation of the superstructure to move loads in a horizontal direction about the axis of rotation.
items.quote: Swing means the rotation of the superstructure for movement of loads in a horizontal direction about the axis of rotation.

items.definition: The machinery involved in rotating the superstructure.
items.quote: Swing mechanism means the machinery involved in providing rotation of the superstructure.

items.definition: An assembly of ropes and sheaves arranged for hoisting and pulling.
items.quote: Tackle is an assembly of ropes and sheaves arranged for hoisting and pulling.

items.definition: Moving or transporting a crane from one jobsite to another.
items.quote: Transit means the moving or transporting of a crane from one jobsite to another.

items.definition: The function of the machine moving from one location to another on a jobsite.
items.quote: Travel means the function of the machine moving from one location to another, on a jobsite.

items.definition: The machinery involved in providing travel.
items.quote: The travel mechanism is the machinery involved in providing travel.

items.definition: The distance between the centers of the front and rear axles. For a multiple axle assembly, the midpoint of the assembly is taken as the axle center for this measurement.
items.quote: Wheelbase means the distance between centers of front and rear axles. For a multiple axle assembly the axle center for wheelbase measurement is taken as the midpoint of the assembly.

items.definition: A separate hoist rope system with lighter load capacity and higher speed than the main hoist provides.
items.quote: The whipline (auxiliary hoist) is a separate hoist rope system of lighter load capacity and higher speed than provided by the main hoist.

items.definition: A power driven spool for handling loads by means of friction between fiber or wire rope and the spool.
items.quote: A winch head is a power driven spool for handling of loads by means of friction between fiber or wire rope and spool.

items.definition: For determining load ratings, with booms of stipulated lengths at stipulated working radii for the various types of crane mountings, this margin is set by taking a percentage of the loads that will produce tipping or balance with the boom in the least stable direction relative to the mounting.
items.quote: The margin of stability for determination of load ratings, with booms of stipulated lengths at stipulated working radii for the various types of crane mountings, is established by taking a percentage of the loads which will produce a condition of tipping or balance with the boom in the least stable direction, relative to the mounting.

items.definition: In applying the load rating percentages to locomotive cranes, tipping, with or without outriggers, occurs when half of the wheels farthest from the load leave the rail.
items.quote:
(ii) The following stipulations shall govern the application of the values in paragraph (c)(1)(i) of this section for locomotive cranes:
(a) Tipping with or without the use of outriggers occurs when half of the wheels farthest from the load leave the rail.

items.definition: In applying the load rating percentages to locomotive cranes, this is the horizontal distance from a projection of the axis of rotation to the rail support surface, taken before loading, to the center of the vertical hoist line or tackle with the load applied.
items.quote:
(ii) The following stipulations shall govern the application of the values in paragraph (c)(1)(i) of this section for locomotive cranes:
(a) Tipping with or without the use of outriggers occurs when half of the wheels farthest from the load leave the rail.
(b) The crane shall be standing on track which is level within 1 percent grade.
(c) Radius of the load is the horizontal distance from a projection of the axis of rotation to the rail support surface, before loading, to the center of vertical hoist line or tackle with load applied.

items.definition: One of the two general classes of inspection procedure for cranes in regular service, which are based on how often inspection should be performed. The intervals depend on the nature of the crane's critical components and their exposure to wear, deterioration or malfunction. Frequent inspection is done at daily to monthly intervals.
items.quote:
Inspection procedure for cranes in regular service is divided into two general classifications based upon the intervals at which inspection should be performed. The intervals in turn are dependent upon the nature of the critical components of the crane and the degree of their exposure to wear, deterioration, or malfunction. The two general classifications are herein designated as “frequent” and “periodic”, with respective intervals between inspections as defined below:
(i) Frequent inspection: Daily to monthly intervals.

items.definition: One of the two general classes of inspection procedure for cranes in regular service, which are based on how often inspection should be performed. The intervals depend on the nature of the crane's critical components and their exposure to wear, deterioration or malfunction. Periodic inspection is done at 1- to 12-month intervals, or as the manufacturer specifically recommends.
items.quote:
Inspection procedure for cranes in regular service is divided into two general classifications based upon the intervals at which inspection should be performed. The intervals in turn are dependent upon the nature of the critical components of the crane and the degree of their exposure to wear, deterioration, or malfunction. The two general classifications are herein designated as “frequent” and “periodic”, with respective intervals between inspections as defined below:
(i) Frequent inspection: Daily to monthly intervals.
(ii) Periodic inspection: 1- to 12-month intervals, or as specifically recommended by the manufacturer.

items.definition: The tilt of a sling leg or branch, measured from the horizontal or vertical plane. An angle of five degrees or less from the vertical may be treated as a vertical angle of loading.
items.quote: Angle of loading is the inclination of a leg or branch of a sling measured from the horizontal or vertical plane as shown in Fig. N-184-5; provided that an angle of loading of five degrees or less from the vertical may be considered a vertical angle of loading.

items.definition: A sling setup in which the sling passes under the load and both of its ends, end attachments, eyes or handles are on the hook or a single master link.
items.quote: Basket hitch is a sling configuration whereby the sling is passed under the load and has both ends, end attachments, eyes or handles on the hook or a single master link.

items.definition: A wire rope made by plaiting component wire ropes.
items.quote: Braided wire rope is a wire rope formed by plaiting component wire ropes.

items.definition: A sling made of multiple wire rope legs whose top ends are gathered in a fitting that goes over the lifting hook.
items.quote: Bridle wire rope sling is a sling composed of multiple wire rope legs with the top ends gathered in a fitting that goes over the lifting hook.

items.definition: A wire rope sling made endless by joining the ends of a single length of cable laid rope with one or more metal fittings.
items.quote: Cable laid endless sling-mechanical joint is a wire rope sling made endless by joining the ends of a single length of cable laid rope with one or more metallic fittings.

items.definition: An endless wire rope sling made from one length of rope wrapped six times around a core, which is formed by hand tucking the rope ends inside the six wraps.
items.quote: Cable laid grommet-hand tucked is an endless wire rope sling made from one length of rope wrapped six times around a core formed by hand tucking the ends of the rope inside the six wraps.

items.definition: A wire rope made of six wire ropes wrapped around a fiber or wire rope core.
items.quote: Cable laid rope is a wire rope composed of six wire ropes wrapped around a fiber or wire rope core.

items.definition: A wire rope sling made from cable laid rope, with eyes made by pressing or swaging one or more metal sleeves over the rope junction.
items.quote: Cable laid rope sling-mechanical joint is a wire rope sling made from a cable laid rope with eyes fabricated by pressing or swaging one or more metal sleeves over the rope junction.

items.definition: A sling setup in which one end of the sling passes under the load and through an end attachment, handle or eye on the other end.
items.quote: Choker hitch is a sling configuration with one end of the sling passing under the load and through an end attachment, handle or eye on the other end of the sling.

items.definition: An elastomer or other suitable material applied to a sling or sling component to give it desirable properties.
items.quote: Coating is an elastomer or other suitable material applied to a sling or to a sling component to impart desirable properties.

items.definition: A wire used to join the spirals of metal mesh into a complete fabric.
items.quote: Cross rod is a wire used to join spirals of metal mesh to form a complete fabric. (See Fig. N-184-2.)

items.definition: Selected or assigned by the employer or the employer's representative as qualified to perform specific duties.
items.quote: Designated means selected or assigned by the employer or the employer's representative as being qualified to perform specific duties.

items.definition: A person or organization, including an employer, whose equipment, technical knowledge and skills allow it to perform the same repairs and tests with equal competence as the person or organization it is equated with.
items.quote: Equivalent entity is a person or organization (including an employer) which, by possession of equipment, technical knowledge and skills, can perform with equal competence the same repairs and tests as the person or organization with which it is equated.

items.definition: The flexible part of a metal mesh sling, made up of a series of transverse coils and cross rods.
items.quote: Fabric (metal mesh) is the flexible portion of a metal mesh sling consisting of a series of transverse coils and cross rods.

items.definition: A handle with a handle eye and a slot sized to let a male handle pass through, so that a metal mesh sling can be used in a choker hitch.
items.quote: Female handle (choker) is a handle with a handle eye and a slot of such dimension as to permit passage of a male handle thereby allowing the use of a metal mesh sling in a choker hitch. (See Fig. N-184-1.)

items.definition: An end fitting to which metal mesh fabric is attached.
items.quote: Handle is a terminal fitting to which metal mesh fabric is attached. (See Fig. N-184-1.)

items.definition: An opening in a metal mesh sling handle that is shaped to accept a hook, shackle or other lifting device.
items.quote: Handle eye is an opening in a handle of a metal mesh sling shaped to accept a hook, shackle or other lifting device. (See Fig. N-184-1.)

items.definition: A sling setup in which the sling is fastened to an object or load, either directly to it or around it.
items.quote: Hitch is a sling configuration whereby the sling is fastened to an object or load, either directly to it or around it.

items.definition: A single ring of a chain.
items.quote: Link is a single ring of a chain.

items.definition: A handle with a handle eye.
items.quote: Male handle (triangle) is a handle with a handle eye.

items.definition: A welded alloy steel coupling link used as an intermediate link to join alloy steel chain to master links.
items.quote: Master coupling link is an alloy steel welded coupling link used as an intermediate link to join alloy steel chain to master links. (See Fig. N-184-3.)

items.definition: A forged or welded steel link used to support all the legs of an alloy steel chain sling or wire rope sling.
items.quote: Master link or gathering ring is a forged or welded steel link used to support all members (legs) of an alloy steel chain sling or wire rope sling. (See Fig. N-184-3.)

items.definition: A nonwelded, mechanically closed steel link used to attach items such as master links and hooks to alloy steel chain.
items.quote: Mechanical coupling link is a nonwelded, mechanically closed steel link used to attach master links, hooks, etc., to alloy steel chain.

items.definition: The load applied when performing a proof test.
items.quote: Proof load is the load applied in performance of a proof test.

items.definition: A nondestructive tension test that the sling manufacturer or an equivalent entity performs to verify a sling's construction and workmanship.
items.quote: Proof test is a nondestructive tension test performed by the sling manufacturer or an equivalent entity to verify construction and workmanship of a sling.

items.definition: The maximum working load permitted by the provisions of this section.
items.quote: Rated capacity or working load limit is the maximum working load permitted by the provisions of this section.
items.term: Rated capacity or working load limit

items.definition: The effective length of an alloy steel chain sling, measured from the top bearing surface of the upper end component to the bottom bearing surface of the lower end component.
items.quote: Reach is the effective length of an alloy steel chain sling measured from the top bearing surface of the upper terminal component to the bottom bearing surface of the lower terminal component.

items.definition: The finished edge of synthetic webbing, designed to prevent unraveling.
items.quote: Selvage edge is the finished edge of synthetic webbing designed to prevent unraveling.

items.definition: An assembly that connects the load to the material handling equipment.
items.quote: Sling is an assembly which connects the load to the material handling equipment.

items.definition: A person or organization that assembles sling components into their final form for sale to users.
items.quote: Sling manufacturer is a person or organization that assembles sling components into their final form for sale to users.

items.definition: A single transverse coil that is the basic element from which metal mesh is made.
items.quote: Spiral is a single transverse coil that is the basic element from which metal mesh is fabricated. (See Fig. N-184-2.)

items.definition: A wire rope sling made endless from one length of rope, with the ends joined by one or more metal fittings.
items.quote: Strand laid endless sling-mechanical joint is a wire rope sling made endless from one length of rope with the ends joined by one or more metallic fittings.

items.definition: An endless wire rope sling made from one length of strand wrapped six times around a core, which is formed by hand tucking the strand ends inside the six wraps.
items.quote: Strand laid grommet-hand tucked is an endless wire rope sling made from one length of strand wrapped six times around a core formed by hand tucking the ends of the strand inside the six wraps.

items.definition: A wire rope made with strands, usually six or eight, wrapped around a fiber core, wire strand core or independent wire rope core (IWRC).
items.quote: Strand laid rope is a wire rope made with strands (usually six or eight) wrapped around a fiber core, wire strand core, or independent wire rope core (IWRC).

items.definition: A way of supporting a load with a single, vertical part or leg of the sling.
items.quote: Vertical hitch is a method of supporting a load by a single, vertical part or leg of the sling. (See Fig. N-184-4.)

items.definition: For purposes of the flash-butt welding truck exclusion only, this means railroad equipment that meets the referenced regulatory definition of “roadway maintenance machine” and is used only for railroad track work.
items.quote: For purposes of this paragraph (c)(18), the terms flash-butt welding truck and roadway maintenance machine refer to railroad equipment that meets the definition of “roadway maintenance machine” in 49 CFR 214.7 and is used only for railroad track work.

items.definition: For purposes of the flash-butt welding truck exclusion only, this means railroad equipment that meets the referenced regulatory definition of “roadway maintenance machine” and is used only for railroad track work.
items.quote: For purposes of this paragraph (c)(18), the terms flash-butt welding truck and roadway maintenance machine refer to railroad equipment that meets the definition of “roadway maintenance machine” in 49 CFR 214.7 and is used only for railroad track work.

items.definition: An individual who meets this subpart's requirements for an A/D director. Formal job title and management or non-management status don't matter.
items.quote: A/D director (Assembly/Disassembly director) means an individual who meets this subpart's requirements for an A/D director, irrespective of the person's formal job title or whether the person is non-management or management personnel.

items.definition: A crane whose boom is a series of folding, pin-connected structural members, typically extended or retracted by power from hydraulic cylinders.
items.quote: Articulating crane means a crane whose boom consists of a series of folding, pin connected structural members, typically manipulated to extend or retract by power from hydraulic cylinders.

items.definition: The assembly and/or disassembly of equipment covered by this standard. For tower cranes, “erecting and climbing” replaces “assembly” and “dismantling” replaces “disassembly.” Increasing the crane's height is an erection process, whether it is first erected to full height or climbed in stages.
items.quote: Assembly/Disassembly means the assembly and/or disassembly of equipment covered under this standard. With regard to tower cranes, “erecting and climbing” replaces the term “assembly,” and “dismantling” replaces the term “disassembly.” Regardless of whether the crane is initially erected to its full height or is climbed in stages, the process of increasing the height of the crane is an erection process.

items.definition: A crane used to help assemble or disassemble a crane.
items.quote: Assist crane means a crane used to assist in assembling or disassembling a crane.

items.definition: Any device that expands the range of tasks the equipment can do. Examples include, but are not limited to, an auger, drill, magnet, pile-driver and boom-attached personnel platform.
items.quote: Attachments means any device that expands the range of tasks that can be done by the equipment. Examples include, but are not limited to: An auger, drill, magnet, pile-driver, and boom-attached personnel platform.

items.definition: A signal made by a distinct sound or series of sounds. Examples include, but are not limited to, sounds from a bell, horn or whistle.
items.quote: Audible signal means a signal made by a distinct sound or series of sounds. Examples include, but are not limited to, sounds made by a bell, horn, or whistle.

items.definition: Also called “cribbing”: wood or other material used to support equipment or a component and distribute loads to the ground. It is typically used to support lattice boom sections during assembly/disassembly and under outrigger and stabilizer floats.
items.quote: Blocking (also referred to as “cribbing”) is wood or other material used to support equipment or a component and distribute loads to the ground. It is typically used to support lattice boom sections during assembly/disassembly and under outrigger and stabilizer floats.

items.definition: A single-point adjustable suspension scaffold with a seat or sling, which may be built into a full body harness, designed to support one employee sitting.
items.quote: Boatswain's chair means a single-point adjustable suspension scaffold consisting of a seat or sling (which may be incorporated into a full body harness) designed to support one employee in a sitting position.

items.definition: Means “travel bogie,” which is defined elsewhere in these definitions.
items.quote: Bogie means “travel bogie,” which is defined below.

items.definition: On equipment other than tower cranes, an inclined spar, strut or other long structural member supporting the upper hoisting tackle on a crane or derrick. Typically its length and vertical angle can be varied to gain height, or height and reach, when lifting. Booms can usually be grouped as hydraulically extendible, cantilevered, latticed section, cable supported or articulating types.
items.quote: Boom (equipment other than tower crane) means an inclined spar, strut, or other long structural member which supports the upper hoisting tackle on a crane or derrick. Typically, the length and vertical angle of the boom can be varied to achieve increased height or height and reach when lifting loads. Booms can usually be grouped into general categories of hydraulically extendible, cantilevered type, latticed section, cable supported type or articulating type.

items.definition: On tower cranes, the principal horizontal structure is called a jib if it is fixed and a boom if it can move up and down.
items.quote: Boom (tower cranes): On tower cranes, if the “boom” (i.e., principal horizontal structure) is fixed, it is referred to as a jib; if it is moveable up and down, it is referred to as a boom.

items.definition: A device that measures the boom's angle relative to horizontal.
items.quote: Boom angle indicator means a device which measures the angle of the boom relative to horizontal.

items.definition: Includes a boom hoist disengaging device, shut-off, disconnect, hydraulic relief or kick-outs, an automatic boom stop device, or a derricking limiter. This type of device cuts boom hoist power when the boom reaches a set operating angle, and sets brakes or closes valves so the boom can't lower after power is disengaged.
items.quote: Boom hoist limiting device includes boom hoist disengaging device, boom hoist shut-off, boom hoist disconnect, boom hoist hydraulic relief, boom hoist kick-outs, automatic boom stop device, or derricking limiter. This type of device disengages boom hoist power when the boom reaches a predetermined operating angle. It also sets brakes or closes valves to prevent the boom from lowering after power is disengaged.

items.definition: Indicates the length of the permanent part of the boom, such as by ruled markings on it, or, in some computerized systems, the boom length including extensions or attachments.
items.quote: Boom length indicator indicates the length of the permanent part of the boom (such as ruled markings on the boom) or, as in some computerized systems, the length of the boom with extensions/attachments.

items.definition: Includes boom stops (belly straps with struts/standoff), telescoping boom stops, attachment boom stops and backstops. These devices keep the boom from moving above a certain maximum angle and toppling backward.
items.quote: Boom stop includes boom stops, (belly straps with struts/standoff), telescoping boom stops, attachment boom stops, and backstops. These devices restrict the boom from moving above a certain maximum angle and toppling over backward.

items.definition: A system of pendants, running ropes, sheaves and other hardware that supports the boom tip and controls the boom angle.
items.quote: Boom suspension system means a system of pendants, running ropes, sheaves, and other hardware which supports the boom tip and controls the boom angle.

items.definition: The builder or constructor of equipment.
items.quote: Builder means the builder/constructor of equipment.

items.definition: The point in an object around which its weight is evenly distributed. A support placed under that point could balance the object.
items.quote: Center of gravity: The center of gravity of any object is the point in the object around which its weight is evenly distributed. If you could put a support under that point, you could balance the object on the support.

items.definition: A welder who meets nationally recognized certification requirements applicable to the task being performed.
items.quote: Certified welder means a welder who meets nationally recognized certification requirements applicable to the task being performed.

items.definition: The process of raising a tower crane to a new working height, either by adding tower sections to its top (top climbing) or by a system that raises the entire crane inside the structure (inside climbing).
items.quote: Climbing means the process in which a tower crane is raised to a new working height, either by adding additional tower sections to the top of the crane (top climbing), or by a system in which the entire crane is raised inside the structure (inside climbing).

items.definition: A mechanical device, typically a chain or cable attached at each end, used to help move materials through leverage.
items.quote: Come-a-long means a mechanical device typically consisting of a chain or cable attached at each end that is used to facilitate movement of materials through leverage.

items.definition: Someone who can identify existing and predictable hazards in the surroundings, or working conditions that are unsanitary, hazardous or dangerous to employees, and who is authorized to take prompt corrective measures to eliminate them.
items.quote: Competent person means one who is capable of identifying existing and predictable hazards in the surroundings or working conditions which are unsanitary, hazardous, or dangerous to employees, and who has authorization to take prompt corrective measures to eliminate them.

items.definition: Lowering a load with a mechanical hoist drum device that allows maximum control using the hoist mechanism's gear train or hydraulic components. It requires using the hoist drive motor, rather than the load hoist brake, to lower the load.
items.quote: Controlled load lowering means lowering a load by means of a mechanical hoist drum device that allows a hoisted load to be lowered with maximum control using the gear train or hydraulic components of the hoist mechanism. Controlled load lowering requires the use of the hoist drive motor, rather than the load hoist brake, to lower the load.

items.definition: An employer that is a prime contractor, general contractor, construction manager or any other legal entity with overall responsibility for the project's construction, including its planning, quality and completion.
items.quote: Controlling entity means an employer that is a prime contractor, general contractor, construction manager or any other legal entity which has the overall responsibility for the construction of the project—its planning, quality and completion.

items.definition: A weight that supplements the equipment's weight to provide stability for lifting loads by counterbalancing them.
items.quote: Counterweight means a weight used to supplement the weight of equipment in providing stability for lifting loads by counterbalancing those loads.

items.definition: Includes all equipment covered by this subpart.
items.quote: Crane/derrick includes all equipment covered by this subpart.

items.definition: Equipment with a type of base mounting that incorporates a continuous belt of sprocket-driven track.
items.quote: Crawler crane means equipment that has a type of base mounting which incorporates a continuous belt of sprocket driven track.

items.definition: Locations on a wire rope spooled on a drum where one layer of rope climbs up and crosses over the previous layer. This happens at each drum flange as the spooling rope reaches it and begins to wrap back the other way.
items.quote: Crossover points means locations on a wire rope which is spooled on a drum where one layer of rope climbs up on and crosses over the previous layer. This takes place at each flange of the drum as the rope is spooled onto the drum, reaches the flange, and begins to wrap back in the opposite direction.

items.definition: A communication line that the employer controlling the communication system assigns to only one signal person and crane/derrick, or to a coordinated group of cranes/derricks and signal person(s).
items.quote: Dedicated channel means a line of communication assigned by the employer who controls the communication system to only one signal person and crane/derrick or to a coordinated group of cranes/derricks/signal person(s).

items.definition: A machine designed to function exclusively as a pile-driver. These machines typically can both hoist the material to be pile-driven and pile-drive it.
items.quote: Dedicated pile-driver is a machine that is designed to function exclusively as a pile-driver. These machines typically have the ability to both hoist the material that will be pile-driven and to pile-drive that material.

items.definition: For power lines, a dedicated spotter must meet the Signal person qualifications requirements. Their sole responsibility is to watch the separation between the power line and the equipment, load line and load (including rigging and lifting accessories) and, by communicating with the operator, ensure the applicable minimum approach distance is not breached.
items.quote: Dedicated spotter (power lines): To be considered a dedicated spotter, the requirements of § 1926.1428 (Signal person qualifications) must be met and his/her sole responsibility is to watch the separation between the power line and the equipment, load line and load (including rigging and lifting accessories), and ensure through communication with the operator that the applicable minimum approach distance is not breached.

items.definition: Part or all of an employee is directly beneath the load.
items.quote: Directly under the load means a part or all of an employee is directly beneath the load.

items.definition: Includes partial dismantling, such as dismantling to shorten a boom or substitute a different component.
items.quote: Dismantling includes partial dismantling (such as dismantling to shorten a boom or substitute a different component).

items.definition: A device on a crane or hoist that shows which direction, and at what relative speed, a particular hoist drum is turning.
items.quote: Drum rotation indicator means a device on a crane or hoist which indicates in which direction and at what relative speed a particular hoist drum is turning.

items.definition: Occurs when a person, object or equipment touches or comes close to an energized conductor or equipment that allows current to pass.
items.quote: Electrical contact occurs when a person, object, or equipment makes contact or comes in close proximity with an energized conductor or equipment that allows the passage of current.

items.definition: Floating cranes/derricks that an employer designed and built for its own use.
items.quote: Employer-made equipment means floating cranes/derricks designed and built by an employer for the employer's own use.

items.definition: Any part of the crane, load line or load (including rigging and lifting accessories) breaching a minimum clearance distance from a power line that this subpart requires.
items.quote: Encroachment is where any part of the crane, load line or load (including rigging and lifting accessories) breaches a minimum clearance distance that this subpart requires to be maintained from a power line.

items.definition: Equipment covered by this subpart.
items.quote: Equipment means equipment covered by this subpart.

items.definition: Instructions, recommendations, limitations and specifications.
items.quote: Equipment criteria means instructions, recommendations, limitations and specifications.

items.definition: Guardrail systems, safety net systems, personal fall arrest systems, positioning device systems or fall restraint systems.
items.quote: Fall protection equipment means guardrail systems, safety net systems, personal fall arrest systems, positioning device systems or fall restraint systems.

items.definition: A fall protection system that prevents the user from falling any distance. It consists of a body belt or body harness plus an anchorage, connectors and other necessary equipment. Other components typically include a lanyard and may include a lifeline and other devices.
items.quote: Fall restraint system means a fall protection system that prevents the user from falling any distance. The system is comprised of either a body belt or body harness, along with an anchorage, connectors and other necessary equipment. The other components typically include a lanyard, and may also include a lifeline and other devices.

items.definition: The area, including but not limited to the area directly beneath the load, where it is reasonably foreseeable that partially or completely suspended materials could fall in an accident.
items.quote: Fall zone means the area (including but not limited to the area directly beneath the load) in which it is reasonably foreseeable that partially or completely suspended materials could fall in the event of an accident.

items.definition: Points of contact between rope and drum flange where the rope changes layers.
items.quote: Flange points are points of contact between rope and drum flange where the rope changes layers.

items.definition: Equipment the manufacturer or employer designed for marine use by permanent attachment to a barge, pontoons, vessel or other means of flotation.
items.quote: Floating cranes/derricks means equipment designed by the manufacturer (or employer) for marine use by permanent attachment to a barge, pontoons, vessel or other means of flotation.

items.definition: “One example, although there are others.”
items.quote: For example means “one example, although there are others.”

items.definition: Only the brake regulates the load line's descent; the drive mechanism is not used to drive the load down faster or slow its lowering.
items.quote: Free fall (of the load line) means that only the brake is used to regulate the descent of the load line (the drive mechanism is not used to drive the load down faster or retard its lowering).

items.definition: The uncontrolled transverse movement of liquids in compartments, which reduces a vessel's transverse stability.
items.quote: Free surface effect is the uncontrolled transverse movement of liquids in compartments which reduce a vessel's transverse stability.

items.definition: A mechanical device that lifts and lowers loads by winding a line onto or off a drum.
items.quote: Hoist means a mechanical device for lifting and lowering loads by winding a line onto or off a drum.

items.definition: Raising, lowering or otherwise moving a load in the air with equipment covered by this standard. Here it can be done by means other than wire rope/hoist drum equipment.
items.quote: Hoisting is the act of raising, lowering or otherwise moving a load in the air with equipment covered by this standard. As used in this standard, “hoisting” can be done by means other than wire rope/hoist drum equipment.

items.definition: “Including, but not limited to.”
items.quote: Include/including means “including, but not limited to.”

items.definition: An insulating device listed, labeled or accepted by a Nationally Recognized Testing Laboratory in accordance with 29 CFR 1910.7.
items.quote: Insulating link/device means an insulating device listed, labeled, or accepted by a Nationally Recognized Testing Laboratory in accordance with 29 CFR 1910.7.

items.definition: Also called a jib backstop: the same type of device as a boom stop, but for a fixed or luffing jib.
items.quote: Jib stop (also referred to as a jib backstop), is the same type of device as a boom stop but is for a fixed or luffing jib.

items.definition: Equipment the manufacturer did not originally design for marine use by permanent attachment to barges, pontoons, vessels or other means of floatation.
items.quote: Land crane/derrick is equipment not originally designed by the manufacturer for marine use by permanent attachment to barges, pontoons, vessels, or other means of floatation.

items.definition: The angle of inclination about the longitudinal axis of a barge, pontoons, vessel or other means of floatation.
items.quote: List means the angle of inclination about the longitudinal axis of a barge, pontoons, vessel or other means of floatation.

items.definition: The object(s) being hoisted and/or their weight. Both uses refer to the object(s) and the load-attaching equipment, such as the load block, ropes, slings, shackles and any other ancillary attachment.
items.quote: Load refers to the object(s) being hoisted and/or the weight of the object(s); both uses refer to the object(s) and the load-attaching equipment, such as, the load block, ropes, slings, shackles, and any other ancillary attachment.

items.definition: A system that aids the equipment operator by directly or indirectly sensing the overturning moment on the equipment (load multiplied by radius), compares this to rated capacity, and shows the operator the percentage of capacity in use. It may include lights, bells or buzzers to warn of an approaching overload.
items.quote: Load moment (or rated capacity) indicator means a system which aids the equipment operator by sensing (directly or indirectly) the overturning moment on the equipment, i.e., load multiplied by radius. It compares this lifting condition to the equipment's rated capacity, and indicates to the operator the percentage of capacity at which the equipment is working. Lights, bells, or buzzers may be incorporated as a warning of an approaching overload condition.

items.definition: A system that aids the operator by directly or indirectly sensing the overturning moment (load multiplied by radius), compares it to rated capacity, and at rated capacity cuts power to functions that can increase loading severity, such as hoisting, telescoping out or luffing out. Functions that reduce it, such as lowering, telescoping in or luffing in, typically remain operational.
items.quote: Load moment (or rated capacity) limiter means a system which aids the equipment operator by sensing (directly or indirectly) the overturning moment on the equipment, i.e., load multiplied by radius. It compares this lifting condition to the equipment's rated capacity, and when the rated capacity is reached, it shuts off power to those equipment functions which can increase the severity of loading on the equipment, e.g., hoisting, telescoping out, or luffing out. Typically, those functions which decrease the severity of loading on the equipment remain operational, e.g., lowering, telescoping in, or luffing in.

items.definition: A crane mounted on a base or car equipped to travel on a railroad track.
items.quote: Locomotive crane means a crane mounted on a base or car equipped for travel on a railroad track.

items.definition: A device similar to a boom hoist limiting device, except that it limits movement of the luffing jib.
items.quote: Luffing jib limiting device is similar to a boom hoist limiting device, except that it limits the movement of the luffing jib.

items.definition: A device, such as a "transfer net," designed to protect employees hoisted during a marine transfer and to allow rapid entry and exit. It does not include boatswain's chairs when hoisted by equipment covered by this standard.
items.quote: Marine hoisted personnel transfer device means a device, such as a “transfer net,” that is designed to protect the employees being hoisted during a marine transfer and to facilitate rapid entry into and exit from the device. Such devices do not include boatswain's chairs when hoisted by equipment covered by this standard.

items.definition: A construction worksite located in, on or above water.
items.quote: Marine worksite means a construction worksite located in, on or above the water.

items.definition: A lifting device with a cable-suspended latticed boom or hydraulic telescopic boom, designed to be moved between operating locations by transport over the road.
items.quote: Mobile crane means a lifting device incorporating a cable suspended latticed boom or hydraulic telescopic boom designed to be moved between operating locations by transport over the road.

items.definition: The times during which an employee is going to or from a work station.
items.quote: Moving point-to-point means the times during which an employee is in the process of going to or from a work station.

items.definition: A machine designed for various configurations, at least one of which lets it hoist (by winch or hook) and horizontally move a suspended load, such as a rotating machine that takes forks/tongs, a winch pack, or a jib. With forks/tongs it is not covered by this subpart; with a winch pack, a jib with an end hook, or a jib used with a winch, it is covered.
items.quote: Multi-purpose machine means a machine that is designed to be configured in various ways, at least one of which allows it to hoist (by means of a winch or hook) and horizontally move a suspended load. For example, a machine that can rotate and can be configured with removable forks/tongs (for use as a forklift) or with a winch pack, jib (with a hook at the end) or jib used in conjunction with a winch. When configured with the forks/tongs, it is not covered by this subpart. When configured with a winch pack, jib (with a hook at the end) or jib used in conjunction with a winch, it is covered by this subpart.

items.definition: An organization widely recognized, due to its independence and expertise, as competent to accredit testing organizations. Examples include, but are not limited to, the National Commission for Certifying Agencies and the American National Standards Institute.
items.quote: Nationally recognized accrediting agency is an organization that, due to its independence and expertise, is widely recognized as competent to accredit testing organizations. Examples of such accrediting agencies include, but are not limited to, the National Commission for Certifying Agencies and the American National Standards Institute.

items.definition: Describes an object that, because of its materials and conditions of use (including environmental conditions and material condition), will not become energized. That is, it has high dielectric properties that strongly resist current under those conditions of use.
items.quote: Nonconductive means that, because of the nature and condition of the materials used, and the conditions of use (including environmental conditions and condition of the material), the object in question has the property of not becoming energized (that is, it has high dielectric properties offering a high resistance to the passage of current under the conditions of use).

items.definition: Devices that help the operator run the crane safely by providing information or automatically taking control of a crane function. They include, but are not limited to, the "listed operational aids."
items.quote: Operational aids are devices that assist the operator in the safe operation of the crane by providing information or automatically taking control of a crane function. These include, but are not limited to, the devices listed in § 1926.1416 (“listed operational aids”).

items.definition: Levers, switches, pedals and other devices for controlling equipment operation.
items.quote: Operational controls means levers, switches, pedals and other devices for controlling equipment operation.

items.definition: A person who is operating the equipment.
items.quote: Operator means a person who is operating the equipment.

items.definition: Includes overhead/bridge, semigantry, cantilever gantry, wall, storage bridge and launching gantry cranes and similar equipment, whether it travels on tracks, wheels or other means.
items.quote: Overhead and gantry cranes includes overhead/bridge cranes, semigantry, cantilever gantry, wall cranes, storage bridge cranes, launching gantry cranes, and similar equipment, irrespective of whether it travels on tracks, wheels, or other means.

items.definition: Unless otherwise specified, a paragraph in the same section of this subpart where the word "paragraph" is used.
items.quote: Paragraph refers to a paragraph in the same section of this subpart that the word “paragraph” is used, unless otherwise specified.

items.definition: Includes wire type (a fixed length of wire rope with mechanical fittings at both ends for pinning rope segments together) and bar type (a bar instead of wire rope). They are typically used in latticed boom crane systems to easily change the boom suspension system's length without completely changing the drum rope when boom length changes.
items.quote: Pendants includes both wire and bar types. Wire type: A fixed length of wire rope with mechanical fittings at both ends for pinning segments of wire rope together. Bar type: Instead of wire rope, a bar is used. Pendants are typically used in a latticed boom crane system to easily change the length of the boom suspension system without completely changing the rope on the drum when the boom length is increased or decreased.

items.definition: A system used to arrest an employee falling from a working level. It consists of an anchorage, connectors and a body harness, and may include a lanyard, deceleration device, lifeline or a suitable combination of these.
items.quote: Personal fall arrest system means a system used to arrest an employee in a fall from a working level. It consists of an anchorage, connectors, a body harness and may include a lanyard, deceleration device, lifeline, or suitable combination of these.

items.definition: A crane with a rotating upperstructure, hoist machinery and boom on top of a structural gantry that may be fixed or able to travel. The gantry legs or columns usually have portal openings between them so traffic can pass beneath.
items.quote: Portal crane is a type of crane consisting of a rotating upperstructure, hoist machinery, and boom mounted on top of a structural gantry which may be fixed in one location or have travel capability. The gantry legs or columns usually have portal openings in between to allow passage of traffic beneath the gantry.

items.definition: Electric transmission and distribution lines.
items.quote: Power lines means electric transmission and distribution lines.

items.definition: Includes, but is not limited to, instructions, diagrams, recommendations, warnings, specifications, protocols and limitations.
items.quote: Procedures include, but are not limited to: Instructions, diagrams, recommendations, warnings, specifications, protocols and limitations.

items.definition: A device that warns of proximity to a power line and has been listed, labeled or accepted by a Nationally Recognized Testing Laboratory in accordance with 29 CFR 1910.7.
items.quote: Proximity alarm is a device that provides a warning of proximity to a power line and that has been listed, labeled, or accepted by a Nationally Recognized Testing Laboratory in accordance with 29 CFR 1910.7.

items.definition: A person employed by the signal person's employer who has demonstrated competence in accurately assessing whether individuals meet this subpart's signal person Qualification Requirements.
items.quote: Qualified evaluator (not a third party) means a person employed by the signal person's employer who has demonstrated that he/she is competent in accurately assessing whether individuals meet the Qualification Requirements in this subpart for a signal person.

items.definition: An entity that, due to its independence and expertise, has demonstrated competence in accurately assessing whether individuals meet this subpart's signal person Qualification Requirements.
items.quote: Qualified evaluator (third party) means an entity that, due to its independence and expertise, has demonstrated that it is competent in accurately assessing whether individuals meet the Qualification Requirements in this subpart for a signal person.

items.definition: A person who has successfully demonstrated the ability to solve problems relating to the subject matter, work or project, through a recognized degree, certificate or professional standing, or through extensive knowledge, training and experience.
items.quote: Qualified person means a person who, by possession of a recognized degree, certificate, or professional standing, or who by extensive knowledge, training and experience, successfully demonstrated the ability to solve/resolve problems relating to the subject matter, the work, or the project.

items.definition: A rigger who meets the criteria for a qualified person.
items.quote: Qualified rigger is a rigger who meets the criteria for a qualified person.

items.definition: A device the equipment operator can set to limit movement of the boom or jib tip to a plane or multiple planes.
items.quote: Range control limit device is a device that can be set by an equipment operator to limit movement of the boom or jib tip to a plane or multiple planes.

items.definition: A device the equipment operator can set to warn that the boom or jib tip is at a plane or multiple planes.
items.quote: Range control warning device is a device that can be set by an equipment operator to warn that the boom or jib tip is at a plane or multiple planes.

items.definition: The maximum working load the manufacturer permits under specified working conditions. These typically include a specific combination of factors such as equipment configuration, radii, boom length and other use parameters.
